Rodriguez was previously Venezuela’s vice president. headlines.full_text: Street theater artists honor Shajareh Tayyebeh martyred students at 20th Resistance Theater Festival TEHRAN – The first day of the street theater performances of the “Sardar-e Asemani” (Heavenly Commander) section at the 20th International Resistance Theater Festival was held in the courtyard of City Theater, Enghelab Square, and Vali-e-Asr (AS) Square in Tehran, featuring seven performing groups and the participation of enthusiastic spectators. TEHRAN – The first day of the street theater performances of the “Sardar-e Asemani” (Heavenly Commander) section at the 20th International Resistance Theater Festival was held in the courtyard of City Theater, Enghelab Square, and Vali-e-Asr (AS) Square in Tehran, featuring seven performing groups and the participation of enthusiastic spectators. On the opening day, artists paid tribute to the students and staff of Shajareh Tayyebeh school in Minab, who were martyred in an attack by the US in February, Mehr reported. The artists aimed to reaffirm that the tragedy of the martyrdom of Iran’s children at the hands of American-Zionist enemies will never be erased from the memory of the artistic community and the people of this land. Through their creative perspectives, the street theater artists sought to narrate themes of martyrdom, resistance, and the steadfastness of the children, women, and men of Iran—particularly regarding the 12-Day War and the Ramadan War. By addressing fresh subjects drawn from social events and political crises, they aimed to engage and connect with the audience. The 20th International Resistance Theater Festival, held under the theme “Iran, the Eternal Stage of Resistance,” is directed by Mohammad Kazemtabar. TEHRAN – Iran’s borders remain fully secure despite mounting pressure and hostile efforts to undermine the country’s stability, Commander of Iran’s Border Guard Command Brigadier General Ali Akbar Javidan said on Wednesday, stressing that adversaries would not be allowed to achieve their objectives. Speaking at a ceremony in Birjand, the capital of South Khorasan Province, Javidan said the country’s security was the result of the round-the-clock efforts of border guards, supported by close cooperation with the Army, Iran’s Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC), and other military and law enforcement forces. He noted that Iran had faced many conspiracies and security threats since the victory of the 1979 Islamic Revolution, adding that the country was now confronting direct pressure from the 'front of global arrogance and the Israeli regime.' According to Javidan, the adversaries are seeking to weaken the Islamic Republic, fuel public discontent and create conditions conducive to insecurity and instability. He stressed, however, that their objectives had been thwarted by public participation, the strength and preparedness of Iran’s Armed Forces, and the effective management of the country’s officials. Javidan’s remarks underscore the importance of integrated security arrangements and inter-agency coordination in safeguarding Iran’s borders against external threats and maintaining stability in border regions.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The border guard chief frames external adversaries, especially the Israeli regime, as conspirators undermining national security.

Now, Brussels estimates that the Ukrainian budget gap would grow to €70 billion next year. The proposed loan is designed to fill around two thirds of this gap. According to the proposal, the loan would be financed through EU joint borrowing on capital markets. The Pentagon last had three carrier strike groups in the region simultaneously in April, for the first time since 2003. Read Full Article at RT.com Russian President Vladimir Putin has accused former global hegemons of resistance to the emergence of a more equitable world order. He condemned their efforts to hold back successful developing nations rather than adapt to shifting economic realities. In his address to the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, China on Wednesday, Putin said the global economy had undergone a“tectonic shift,”in which the Asia-Pacific region has emerged as the planet’s leading technological hub. He heralded the Asian economies which were once the“world’s factory”as major drivers of innovation. Over the past 35 years, the share of developing and emerging-market economies in global output has nearly doubled, rising from 35% in 1990 to 61% in 2026, Putin noted. “It was here, in the Asia-Pacific region, that the fundamental changes now spreading across the world like waves first originated,”he said. The regional economic model demonstrates how a“fairer, more democratic and equitable world order”is taking shape, he argued, with traditional hierarchical structures giving way to new horizontal relationships between nations. “However, these inevitable changes, this shift in the center of gravity of the global economic balance, are not always adequately perceived,”Putin said. headlines.llm_reasoning: The speech frames Russia as a champion against entrenched powers, positioning it as a moral counterweight.

headlines.title: US spy agency’s classified communications network goes down

US spy agency’s classified communications network goes down The NSA reported a temporary degradation of its internal systems during routine maintenance amid a wave of technical failures across the US
Read Full Article at RT.com The US National Security Agency (NSA) has reportedly suffered an outage of its highly classified internal communications network, which disrupted the work of intelligence personnel and forced employees to adjust their schedules. The incident is the latest in a string of major technical failures affecting American government infrastructure, airlines, banks and technology giants. The disruption affected NSANet, the agency’s primary internal network for exchanging classified information, including top-secret intelligence. The outage was first reported on Tuesday by CNN, which cited six people familiar with the matter, and was subsequently corroborated by several major US media outlets. The NSA later acknowledged problems with its internal systems but downplayed their impact, insisting that its most critical operations had not been compromised. “The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance,”the agency said in a statement. “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues,”it added, stressing that multiple layers of backup infrastructure were in place to maintain essential operations. The outage prompted a“code yellow”alert at the agency’s headquarters in Fort Meade, Maryland, according to the New York Times. headlines.llm_reasoning: The article simply reports the NSA outage and its context without any emotive or biased framing.

headlines.raw_title: US strikes Iran in ‘self-defense’
headlines.title: US strikes Iran in ‘self-defense’
headlines.full_text:
US strikes Iran in ‘self-defense’ The attack on Qeshm Island comes hours after the IRGC targeted an American military radar installation in Bahrain
Read Full Article at RT.com US fighter jets have struck an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz in what Washington has described as an act of“self-defense.” The attack came hours after Tehran launched drones against an American military installation in Bahrain. “Earlier today, US fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense,”a US military official told reporters on Tuesday. “The strike was in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets,”the official added, saying that US Central Command (CENTCOM) remains fully prepared to protect American forces across the region. The Pentagon did not specify which Iranian action prompted the strike. However, the attack followed an IRGC drone operation against a US radar installation at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain earlier on Tuesday – the third such attack on American military targets in the tiny island kingdom in five days. Tehran described the operation as retaliation for repeated violations of Iranian airspace by American military drones. Bahrain said it had intercepted the incoming aircraft, while CENTCOM said the attack had been thwarted. Iranian authorities confirmed that US forces had attacked several locations on Qeshm Island. Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Hormozgan Province, said the strikes caused no damage to residential or commercial areas or civilian infrastructu
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece frames the US strike on Iran as a necessary act of self‑defense, presenting it as justified military action.

headlines.raw_title: European leaders finally remember the EU isn’t a country

headlines.full_text:
European leaders finally remember the EU isn’t a country One voice for Europe at the Ukraine peace deal table isn’t very democratic

Five countries want to represent Europe at Ukraine peace negotiations with Russia and the US. For once, their teenage-girl bathroom-break format is actually a good thing. At least for democracy. But also for any eventual treaty, however counterintuitively. Every interested party gets a delegation. Europe has decided that France, the UK, Italy, Poland, and Germany will comprise its own – along with a couple of representatives from EU institutions. So what’s the problem? Other negotiating parties – notably Russia and the US – have called for the appointment of a single European representative. This would be convenient for negotiating purposes, but hardly a substitute for democratic and constitutional authority. We’re talking about 27 EU member states, plus a wider circle of non-EU European countries. They’re already issued aformal declarationdetailing their common position in black and white, but a single position shouldn’t be conflated with the need for a single representative empowered to commit them all. Negotiations with a single representative might go more smoothly than with a delegation – right up until ratification. headlines.llm_reasoning: The article selectively emphasizes the EU’s lack of democratic representation to undermine its legitimacy.

headlines.full_text:

Newsrooms across the globe are closely following this gathering. Many Western media outlets have rushed to frame the upcoming talks as“a second Yalta.”Yet what they overlook above all is that the underlying theme of our times has fundamentally changed. In 1945, the world was just emerging from the devastation of WWII. Within that historical context, major powers’ attempts to carve out spheres of influence through military power, while far from legitimate, gained a degree of acceptance under the prevailing international order of that era. headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece celebrates the Shenzhen meeting as a symbol of cooperation, elevating national prestige.

It was an attempted coup,”Yair Lapid, who led the opposition in the previous parliament, wrote on X on Monday. The accusations follow an investigation aired by Israel’s Channel 12 on Sunday, alleging that Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, had tipped off police about supposed vote-buying by members of the Arab-led Ra’am party ahead of the October 27 election. headlines.title: United Airlines hit by outage amid widespread US banking disruptions
headlines.full_text:
United Airlines hit by outage amid widespread US banking disruptions Thousands of customers reported problems accessing accounts and transferring money, with JPMorgan Chase blaming a technical glitch
Read Full Article at RT.com US carrier United Airlines has suffered a systemwide technology outage which disrupted hundreds of flights on Monday, as thousands of Americans simultaneously reported problems accessing their bank accounts and transferring money. The incidents mark the latest in a string of major technical failures affecting US aviation, banking and communications infrastructure in recent days. United Airlines said the malfunction affected departing flights across its network, while aircraft already in the air and flights operated by its United Express regional affiliates were unaffected. “We’re aware of the widespread system outage, and our teams are working hard to get things back up and running as soon as possible,”the airline said in a statement, apologizing to passengers. Flight-tracking website FlightAware recorded at least 418 delayed United flights by late Monday afternoon. At Houston’s George Bush Intercontinental Airport, a pilot was heard asking air traffic controllers for permission to remain at the gate until the system was restored, according to a recording cited by the Associated Press. Earlier today we experienced a technology-related issue that impacted some departing flights. The issue has been resolved. Please check the latest status of your flight at https://t.co/BqzX0dcUna or the United app. United Airlines later confirmed that the outage had been resolved, adding that there was no indication of a cyberattack. The airline did not disclose the cause of the malfunctio

headlines.raw_title: Strengthening Russian transit infrastructure offers new prospects for Asia Pacific — Putin
headlines.title: Strengthening Russian transit infrastructure offers new prospects for Asia Pacific — Putin
headlines.full_text: Strengthening Russian transit infrastructure offers new prospects for Asia Pacific — Putin Russia, according to the president, invites all the economics of the region to take advantage of the opportunities offered by these new logistics routes SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. The strengthening of Russia’s transit transport infrastructure opens up new prospects for cooperation within the Asia Pacific region, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the APEC summit plenary session. "Russia's strengthening its transit transport infrastructure based on our country's eastern railway network, the North-South multimodal corridor, and the Northern Sea Route opens up new prospects for cooperation within the Asia Pacific region," he said. Russia, according to Putin, invites all the economics of the region to take advantage of the opportunities offered by these new logistics routes. "Some of our partners have already begun this work. We welcome this and will support it in every possible way," he pledged.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article praises Russia’s transit infrastructure as a boon for Asia Pacific, highlighting national achievements.

headlines.title: Houthis say Saudi-led coalition struck Sanaa, two Yemeni governorates
headlines.full_text: Houthis say Saudi-led coalition struck Sanaa, two Yemeni governorates The SABA agency reported that a medical center was damaged in Taiz DOHA, November 19. /TASS/. The Saudi-led coalition has delivered airstrikes on Yemen’s capital city of Sanaa and two more Yemeni governorates, the Houthi-controlledSABAagency reported. According to the agency, the attacks targeted the city of Sanaa, and the Saada and Taiz governorates. A medical center was damaged in Taiz, it said. headlines.raw_title: Putin highly praises China’s efforts as APEC chair
headlines.title: Putin highly praises China’s efforts as APEC chair
headlines.full_text: Putin highly praises China’s efforts as APEC chair Concluding his speech at the APEC plenary session, the Russian leader thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping and all his Chinese friends for their hospitality and productive joint work SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed his highest praise for the work of China, which is chairing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) in 2026. "First and foremost, I would like to express my highest praise for China’s work as the APEC chair this year. We fully endorse the slogan of the Chinese chairmanship: 'Forging Ahead with Resolve Toward a Bright Future for the Asia-Pacific’," Putin said at the plenary session of the APEC summit. "This is a massive task, one that APEC, as the largest economic forum in our shared macro-region, is well-equipped to tackle," he added. Concluding his speech at the APEC plenary session, the Russian leader thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping and all his Chinese friends for their hospitality and productive joint work. "And I wish Vietnam success as it assumes the APEC chairmanship in 2027," Putin stressed.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece praises China’s role as APEC chair, framing it as a moral and strategic success.

headlines.raw_title: Russia implemented over 80 projects with its APEC partners in past decades — Putin
headlines.title: Russia implemented over 80 projects with its APEC partners in past decades — Putin
headlines.full_text: Russia implemented over 80 projects with its APEC partners in past decades — Putin The president pledged that Russia will continue to take an active part in APEC’s work SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Russia and its partners in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) have implemented more than 80 major projects over recent decades, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the APEC plenary session. He pledged that Russia will continue to take an active part in APEC’s work. "We will continue to work together with our partners in the forum to implement joint, mutually beneficial projects and initiatives. Over the past decades, more than 80 such projects have been implemented, and I am referring only to large-scale ones, including in the areas of agricultural production and trade, the e-government services, and women’s entrepreneurship," he said, adding that since 2015, Russia has been holding an annual competition for women’s entrepreneurial projects.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It emphasizes Russia’s extensive project record with APEC partners to showcase national competence.

headlines.title: Russia’s GDP up by over 10% in real terms over past three years — Putin

headlines.title: Putin says partnership with Asia Pacific economies is Russia’s strategic priority

Russia’s strategic priority is to develop constructive partnership with the economies of the Asia-Pacific region, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the plenary session of the APEC summit. "I would like to emphasize that a constructive partnership with the economies of the Asia Pacific region is Russia’s strategic course. We are an integral part of the region and contribute much to its economic prosperity," he said.

headlines.raw_title: Russia carries out fundamental reforms in its economy — Putin
headlines.title: Russia carries out fundamental reforms in its economy — Putin
headlines.full_text: Russia carries out fundamental reforms in its economy — Putin The Russian president added that the reforms are aimed at improving the industrial base and technological capabilities and controlling inflation SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Russia is implementing fundamental reforms in its economy, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the plenary session of the APEC summit. He emphasized that Russia remains open to the world while simultaneously strengthening its economic potential. "To this end, we continue to implement fundamental reforms at home to improve our industrial base and technological capabilities, and control inflation. We have radically changed the structure of Russia’s domestic economy," he said. According to the president, Russia is also prioritizing the development of cutting-edge industries, such as digital technologies, artificial intelligence, and nuclear energy.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece presents Putin's remarks on economic reforms in a straightforward, factual manner.

headlines.raw_title: Russia supports draft APEC summit final declaration — Putin
headlines.title: Russia supports draft APEC summit final declaration — Putin
headlines.full_text: Russia supports draft APEC summit final declaration — Putin The Russian leader noted that in today’s challenging conditions, the APEC forum must set a unifying tone and establish a constructive agenda for cooperation SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Moscow supports the draft final declaration of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Russian President Vladimir Putin said while addressing the summit’s plenary session. The Russian leader noted that in today’s challenging conditions, marked by the fragmentation of the global economy and mounting challenges and threats to its stability, the APEC forum must set a unifying tone and establish a constructive agenda for cooperation. "This is precisely the aim of the draft Shenzhen Declaration prepared for our approval, which Russia supports," Putin emphasized.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It reports Putin's support for the APEC declaration without any evaluative language.

headlines.raw_title: Russia’s trade with Asia Pacific countries grew by third in 8 months of 2026 — Putin
headlines.title: Russia’s trade with Asia Pacific countries grew by third in 8 months of 2026 — Putin
headlines.full_text: Russia’s trade with Asia Pacific countries grew by third in 8 months of 2026 — Putin According to the Russian president, the country's total trade with ASEAN nations has increased by nearly 60% over the past 10 years SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Russia’s trade with Asia Pacific countries grew by nearly a third over the first eight months of 2026, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the APEC summit’s plenary session. "In the first eight months of this year alone, our trade with the region's economies grew by nearly a third, with a focus on non-energy and innovative products," he said. According to Putin, Russia’s total trade with ASEAN countries has increased by nearly 60% over the past 10 years. "I would also like to mention the expanding network of preferential agreements between countries of this region and the Eurasian Economic Union, which includes Russia and our closest neighbors," he added. According to the Russian leader, the Asia Pacific region has become one of the driving forces of global development, demonstrating positive dynamics and a steady pace of growth in its industrial, technological, and logistical capabilities. "According to forecasts, the aggregate economic growth of APEC members this year will amount to 4.8%, which significantly exceeds global figures," Putin added.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article conveys trade statistics and Putin's comments factually, with no framing.

headlines.raw_title: Putin, Trump shake hands again before photo session on day two of APEC summit
headlines.title: Putin, Trump shake hands again before photo session on day two of APEC summit
headlines.full_text: Putin, Trump shake hands again before photo session on day two of APEC summit The presidents exchanged a few words SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Presidents Vladimir Putin of Russia and Donald Trump of the United States shook hands again before a photo session on the second day of the APEC summit, a TASS correspondent reported. As the leaders of the APEC economies lined up for a group photo, Putin walked over to take his place in the front row. At that moment, he and Trump, who was already standing for the photo, greeted each other with a handshake. The American leader patted the Russian president on the shoulder and exchanged a few words with him with a smile, to which Putin nodded amiably and replied.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It describes a handshake event between leaders in a neutral, descriptive tone.

headlines.raw_title: Putin arrives in APEC summit venue
headlines.title: Putin arrives in APEC summit venue
headlines.full_text: Putin arrives in APEC summit venue The Shenzhen International Exchange Center is the main venue for the summit SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin has arrived in Shenzhen International Exchange Center to take part in a plenary session of the APEC summit. The Shenzhen International Exchange Center is the main venue for the APEC summit. It is located in the Futian District within Xiangmi Park. The compound also includes the Shenzhen Financial Culture Center and the International Performance Center. The total floor area of the buildings is approximately 470,000 square meters. The compound is designed to accommodate more than 10,000 people at a time and includes a main hall with an area of approximately 5,000 square meters, a banquet hall with an area of approximately 3,800 square meters, and about 60 meeting rooms of various capacities, as well as hotel accommodations.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article simply reports factual details about Putin's arrival without bias or emotive language.

headlines.title: Trump promises to resolve standoff with Iran soon

headlines.title: Crimean Bridge comes under another attack by Ukrainian troops

headlines.raw_title: Putin did not speak with Musk in Shenzhen — Kremlin spokesman
headlines.title: Putin did not speak with Musk in Shenzhen — Kremlin spokesman
headlines.full_text: Putin did not speak with Musk in Shenzhen — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov added that the Russian president did not meet with the US entrepreneur SHEZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin did not speak with US entrepreneur Elon Musk on the first day of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Putin’s Press Secretary Dmitry Peskov told TASS. Western media reported earlier that Musk was expected to accompany US President Donald Trump at the summit. "No, we did not see him," Peskov said, when asked whether Putin had any contacts with Musk on the summit’s sidelines, and whether they had discussed Starlink and Rassvet. At a formal reception that was held on the first day of the APEC summit, Putin had the opportunity to speak with various foreign representatives. Along with heads of state, the guests included, for example, American economist Jeffrey Sachs.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article corrects earlier reports by stating that Putin did not meet Musk, providing objective facts without bias.

headlines.raw_title: Putin-Xi-Trump meeting in China’s Shenzhen scheduled for 6:30 a.m. GMT
headlines.title: Putin-Xi-Trump meeting in China’s Shenzhen scheduled for 6:30 a.m. GMT
headlines.full_text: Putin-Xi-Trump meeting in China’s Shenzhen scheduled for 6:30 a.m. GMT The talks will be held at the Qilin Shanzhuang state residence SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. The first-ever trilateral meeting between Presidents Vladimir Putin of Russia, Xi Jinping of China, and Donald Trump of the United States is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. local time (6:30 a.m. GMT), a TASS correspondent reported. The talks will be held at the Qilin Shanzhuang state residence in Shenzhen, which hosted full-scale bilateral talks between Putin and Xi. As Russian Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov said earlier, the talks will be attended by the delegations, which have already been agreed upon. However, work on a potential communique continues. The leaders themselves will decide how long their meeting will last. According to Ushakov, the agenda may include a wide range of issues, including "festering" conflicts around the world. Another major topic will be building relations between the largest powers and their influence on the global situation. After the summit, Putin is expected to hold a news conference to brief on his contacts.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It provides the scheduled time and location of the trilateral meeting without any evaluative commentary.

headlines.raw_title: Putin to take part in trilateral meeting with Xi, Trump
headlines.title: Putin to take part in trilateral meeting with Xi, Trump
headlines.full_text: Putin to take part in trilateral meeting with Xi, Trump This will be the first-ever meeting in this format SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. Presidents Vladimir Putin of Russia, Xi Jinping of China, and Donald Trump of the United States will hold a meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit. This will be the first-ever meeting in such format. The Kremlin emphasized that it considers today’s meeting to be very important and has pragmatic expectations for it. According to Russian Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov, the three leaders have plenty of topics to discuss amid the current turbulent global situation, especially since there is no rigid agenda for the talks, and the leaders will be able to exchange views on any issue. A joint communique may be issued following the meeting. However, the main topic of the discussion will be the development of relations among the major powers, Ushakov noted, especially given the positive experience that Moscow, Beijing, and Washington had in 1945 - after their joint victory, when the powers were among the founding members of the United Nations. Of no less importance, according to the Kremlin, is to ensure that the partnership between the world’s largest countries helps improve the global situation as a whole and resolve conflicts - a sort of "abscess" on the body of humanity. One such conflict is taking place in Ukraine, Ushakov noted, saying that "the leaders are unlikely to avoid discussing this issue." At the same time, Moscow believes that the talks in Shenzhen will serve as a starting point for the discussions the US is conducting in Euro
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article outlines the purpose and context of the meeting in a straightforward, balanced manner.

headlines.raw_title: Houthis claim cruise missile strike on airport and financial center in Riyadh
headlines.title: Houthis claim cruise missile strike on airport and financial center in Riyadh
headlines.full_text: Houthis claim cruise missile strike on airport and financial center in Riyadh Spokesman Yahya Saree added that the strikes achieved "accurate and direct hits" DOHA, November 19. /TASS/. Yemen's Houthi rebel movement Ansar Allah launched a cruise missile strike on King Khalid International Airport and a financial center in Riyadh, the rebels' military spokesman Yahya Saree said, according to the Houthi-controlledSABAnews agency. "The armed forces attacked King Khalid International Airport and the financial center in Riyadh using a large number of cruise missiles, with the strikes achieving accurate and direct hits," Saree said. On November 17, the Houthis from Ansar Allah said they had struck two oil pumping stations west of the Saudi capital city. "Our armed forces (Houthi units - TASS) <…> conducted two military operations. The first one involved the use of three drones that attacked oil pumping station 9 on the East-West pipeline west of Riyadh," Saree wrote on his Telegram channel, adding that the second operation targeted oil pumping station 8 on the same pipeline. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its target was the radar system at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, which is home to theU.S. Fifth Fleet. Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted the incoming drones after authorities issued a security alert urging residents to seek shelter. Officials announced an all-clear later in the morning, with no deaths or injuries reported. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) also addressed the Iranian drone strikes, saying they didn't hit their intended target. The drones were "intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel," CENTCOM said. According to CNN, citing the Israeli source, Netanyahu told Kushner that moving ahead with the proposal was "problematic" because of Israel's upcoming elections at the end of October. The source said Netanyahu, who is seeking support from right-wing voters and has been trailing in several polls, has been reluctant to make concessions on Gaza ahead of the elections. Yet, captivating as Mr Huang’s manoeuvres are, the fracas at Nvidia has underscored a deeper, and more consequential tale: China’s hell-for-leather scramble to gain access to the technology behind American artificial intelligence, by whatever means necessary. It offered a sometimes-legal route for Chinese developers to train their models with top-end chips—until November 16th, when America’s Bureau of Industry and Security, the branch of the Commerce Department that runs chip controls, set out a rule restricting the practice. Remote access and smuggling together roughly doubled the compute, or processing power, available to Chinese AI companies from domestic production and legal imports alone, estimates the Institute for Progress, a think-tank. But China wants more than just to get the best chips. It also wishes to build them itself. There aren't many of them,” Trump told Fox News. He did that.’ We have to take care. You know, I helped Elon a lot in my first term. He was in big trouble. And now we have a guy who is sending up rockets and landing them,” Trump added. To some, the trilateral in Shenzhen echoes the fundamental principle behind Yalta: great powers led by strong leaders get to decide the world’s big issues between them while the rest of the world watches. You can change your cookie settings through your browser. Ma Fengjie Copied A sore throat, a runny nose or an earache can disrupt an ordinary day. When symptoms become uncomfortable, some people reach for antibiotics left over from a previous illness, believing they will recover faster. But antibiotics do not work against every infection. If a sore throat is caused by a virus, for example, an antibiotic will not treat the cause. Unnecessary or incorrect use can have consequences far beyond one episode of illness. This everyday decision is connected to a much larger threat: antimicrobial resistance (AMR). As microorganisms become resistant to medicines designed to treat them, infections can become harder to cure. Antibiotic resistance is a major part of this challenge, threatening medicines on which modern healthcare depends. That is why World AMR Awareness Week, observed from November 18 to 24, matters to everyone. Its 2026 theme, "One Health, one action: Prevent AMR now," calls for coordinated action across human, animal and environmental health. World Children's Day on November 20, which falls during this week, reminds us that protecting children’s health also means using antibiotics wisely so that effective medicines remain available for future generations. A mother cares for her sick daughter and gives her medicine. /VCG A threat

Innovators based in China filed about 1.9 million patent applications, followed by the United States with 489,766, Japan with 466,301 and South Korea with 319,210. Save Share NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, the most distant human-made object, has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after it was launched. The spacecraft hit the milestone on Wednesday and is now about 26 billion km away, according to NASA. A light-day is the distance light can travel in 24 hours, which means messages sent from Earth take a day to reach Voyager 1, and another day for teams on the ground to receive a reply. The feat is “the best illustration of just how vast space is”, said NASA scientist Tiffany Kataria. “So much of what we dream about is travelling to other stellar systems,” she told the AFP news agency. “And it took Voyager 1 nearly 50 years to get to just the edge of our own solar system, let alone to only a light-day.” Many exoplanetary systems, she noted, are at least several light-years away. NASA expects Voyager 1 to take about 18,000 years to travel a full light-year. Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 are the only spacecraft to have reached interstellar space, the region beyond the Sun’s heliosphere. Voyager 2 is expected to reach one light-day in 2035. Some of Voyager 1’s equipment, including its cameras, has been switched off remotely to save power, but the probe continues to studyinvisible phenomenasuch as magnetic fields.
